feature_spec.title: OpenCode MIT session/tool/event contract adoption for Shipyard WorkerRuntime
acceptance_criteria: WorkerRuntimeSession separates durable input admission from turn promotion
RuntimeToolRegistry rejects stale tool registrations after scoped replacement
ToolResultNormalizer bounds model-facing summaries while retaining full artifact references
OpenCodeRuntimeEventBridge emits source event count and replay cursor
OpenCode MIT source adoption is documented with explicit non-port scope
assumptions: This slice ports control-plane contracts, not OpenCode TUI/provider registry/slash command runtime
The implementation is adapted to Shipyard's Node/Vitest domain model rather than importing OpenCode's Effect/Bun runtime

observation_set.summary: WorkerRuntime requirements and MIT porting notes define the adopted OpenCode contracts and non-port scope.
Runtime unit tests cover durable input admission, exact retry, promotion, event replay, stale registration rejection, bounded output, and replay cursor.
Full Shipyard test suite passed after the OpenCode MIT runtime contract adoption.

risk_register.summary: License provenance is explicit; direct substantial ports must preserve the OpenCode MIT notice.
Scoped tool registration and stale registration rejection reduce wrong-handler execution risk.
Model-facing output bounding preserves a retained artifact reference and avoids lossy success.

gate_decision.reason: OpenCode MIT runtime contract adoption is documented, implemented, and covered by focused runtime tests plus the full Shipyard test suite for the standard profile.
